fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. The LORD says, “…at the age of fifty, they must retire from performing the work and no longer serve.” Fifty is the line, and the verse calls it a must. That's the end of the work itself, but the very next verse has more to say about what comes after. Keep that in mind, because retirement here isn't the whole story.

That's the one, baker. The LORD tells Moses to say that the seven lamps “…are to light the area in front of the lampstand.” Then Aaron does it, setting up the lamps facing toward the front, just as the LORD had commanded Moses (Numbers 8:3). Aaron follows the instruction exactly as given. That's the whole job done right.

Good guess, friend, but the LORD doesn't mention the ceiling. He says the seven lamps are to light the area in front of the lampstand. Aaron then sets them up facing toward the front, just as the LORD had commanded Moses (Numbers 8:3). So the light goes out front, not up.

Good try, friend, but moving isn't the first thing the LORD asks. He says, “Take the Levites from among the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean.” Later they are brought before the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 8:9), but that comes after the cleansing. Cleansing is step one.

Yes, baker. The LORD says to “…present the Levites before the LORD and have the Israelites lay their hands upon them.” The whole congregation is assembled at the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 8:9), and the Israelites are the ones to lay hands on the Levites. The text doesn't say how it all happens, so I'll leave it right there.

Provision does sound like it belongs near a pile of offerings, friend, but it's not what the LORD says. The Levites lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, and one bull is a sin offering and the other a burnt offering, “…to make atonement for the Levites.” That's the purpose the LORD gives for the two bulls. Atonement is the word.

Skipping offerings is a fair thing to wonder, friend, but the text never says that. The LORD says the Levites serve and make atonement for the Israelites “…so that no plague will come against the Israelites when they approach the sanctuary.” That's the reason He gives. Nothing in these verses changes what the other tribes bring.

That's right, baker. The text says the Levites came to perform their service at the Tent of Meeting “…in the presence of Aaron and his sons.” Those are the people the verse names, so Moses and the elders aren't part of what it says. The verse closes by saying they did with the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Leading is a natural guess, friend, but the verse doesn't say that. The LORD says they “…may assist their brothers in fulfilling their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they themselves are not to do the work.” The word is assist. They stay part of the team in a new way.
